On 27 June 1995 Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the crown prince of Qatar, took power from his father, Emir Khalifa, while the old ruler was abroad in Switzerland.

Hamad had long run the government in practice. As emir he poured the new gas money from the North Field into an ambitious foreign policy. He founded Al Jazeera in 1996, built Education City, and set up a sovereign wealth fund. Qatar hosted a US air base and also kept ties with Iran and Islamist movements.

His neighbours resented the new line, which led to the blockade of 2017. Hamad handed power to his son Tamim in 2013, a rare peaceful abdication in the region.
sum: On 27 June 1995 Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the crown prince of Qatar, took power from his father, Emir Khalifa, while the old ruler was abroad in Switzerland.
